walkthroughs.body_html:
Theme 2: Managing Business Activities — a core area of A-Level Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Theme 2: Managing Business Activities brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Theme 2: Managing Business Activities.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Focus
Innovation
Acquisition

options: Porter
Kim and Mauborgne
Hamel and Prahalad
Drucker

mcqs.q: How does HRM differ from traditional personnel management?
options: HRM and personnel are exactly the same thing — just a name change.
HRM only applies to large multinational companies.
HRM treats people as a strategic asset and integrates human resource policies with business strategy; personnel management is more administrative and reactive, handling hiring, pay and disputes.
Gross profit is profit before VAT and net profit is profit after VAT.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between gross profit and net profit?
options: Share prices are set by the government each morning.
Gross profit = revenue minus cost of goods sold (direct costs only); net profit = revenue minus ALL costs including overheads, interest and tax. Net profit is the bottom line.
Gross profit and net profit are the same thing.
Gross profit is profit before VAT and net profit is profit after VAT.

mcqs.q: Why does a company's share price change?
options: Share prices are set by the government each morning.
Gross profit is profit before VAT and net profit is profit after VAT.
Share prices go up when a company makes more money this year.
Share prices reflect investors' expectations about future profits — driven by company performance, sector trends, economic conditions, and market sentiment.
